title: Autoscaler threshold sensitivity causing small-tenant preemption and reserved-pool shortfalls
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: A sequence of production incidents over the past week where small tenants experienced sudden latency spikes and 503s. Root cause traced to an aggressive threshold sensitivity change in the dedicated autoscaler that caused premature preemption of warm slots for low-cardinality tenants and incorrect replenishment of reserved pool headroom. Symptoms: customer-facing timeouts, elevated token queuing, and rapid depletion of burst credit for affected tenants. Impact: multiple customers reported degraded performance during peak bursts; three enterprise customers opened escalations and one threatened to convert to Dedicated burst guarantees.
comments: 2025-02-18 09:23 - Ava Chen: Triage call summary: observed correlated jump in preempt_count for small tenants starting 2025-02-17 22:00 UTC. Autoscaler metric preempt_sensitivity was increased in runtime-1.18 to reduce queue latency for high-cardinality traffic; unintended side effect for small tenants.

2025-02-18 11:10 - Diego Morales: Reproduced locally with synthetic workload: lowering tenant qps to mimic low-cardinality ramps shows preemptive eviction when headroom delta < 12%. Repro steps captured in doc linked below.

2025-02-19 02:05 - SRE Pager: Incident declared SEV2 for reserved-pool shortfall in us-west-2; emergency mitigation applied: temporary relaxation of preemption window (patch toggled via feature flag).
2025-02-19 04:50 - Product (Leah Patel): Customer comms drafted. Notified three customers with interim mitigation and ETA for permanent fix.

2025-02-20 14:30 - Diego Morales: Hotfix PR opened to introduce tenant-cardinality-aware sensitivity scaling (PR #8764). Includes conservative default for small tenants and telemetry to track preempt decisions.

2025-02-21 09:12 - QA (Ravi Singh): Validated fix in canary region with synthetic and real-traffic replay; observed no regression in high-cardinality tail latency; small-tenant 95th p90 improved and preempt_count normalized.

2025-02-24 16:00 - PM (Leah Patel): Decided rollout plan: staged canary to dedicated clusters by priority, 15-minute evaluation windows, automatic rollback on >3 customer errors or >5% increase in tail latency.

2025-02-26 08:20 - Diego Morales: Canary rollout started in us-west-2; initial 2h window green. Monitoring dashboards created for preempt_count, reserved_headroom, burst_credit_balance, and tenant_error_rate.

2025-02-27 07:45 - Support (Maria Lopez): Customers updated: two customers confirmed restored behavior; one customer still seeing intermittent 503s - routing engineering investigating per-tenant traces.
next_steps: Continue staged rollout to eu-central-1 and ap-southeast-1 with 15-minute windows and automated rollback triggers.
Instrument additional labels on preempt events to capture tenant size and QPS bucket to validate heuristics under production variance.
Follow-up retrospective to decide permanent defaults and add safety net: minimum guaranteed reserved headroom for any tenant > 30 days on Dedicated.
Publish postmortem and remediation checklist after full rollout or rollback completion.
Coordinate with Solutions Engineering to offer affected customers a credits package and post-mortem call.
resolution: in-flight: hotfix deployed to canary and three regions; pending global rollout and final sign-off after 48h of stable telemetry.
